thesis: Chennai in January runs several hundred concerts a day for an audience that lives there.
scene: It's 4:15 and the second kutcheri of the day is starting at a sabha in Mylapore. The hall is two-thirds full, mostly people over sixty, and about a dozen of them are keeping tala on their thighs without looking down. A man in the fourth row has a notebook. Somebody's phone goes off and is silenced with real embarrassment. The violinist is following a line the singer has not finished yet. Outside, the canteen has a queue for filter coffee that will be longer at the interval than the ticket queue was, and the woman at the counter already knows the order.

sceneAnchors.text: The old quarter around the Kapaleeshwarar tank, where several sabhas sit within a few streets of each other and the December-January schedule is printed and argued over. Before dawn in Margazhi the lanes have kolam drawn fresh on the ground outside each door, and by evening the same lanes are full of people walking between halls.

The temporary kitchens run inside the concert societies for the season, staffed by caterers with reputations of their own. People choose between two halls partly on the music and partly on who is cooking. The interval is thirty minutes and the queue understands this. Reviews of the season cover both.

The largest of the societies, on TTK Road, where the afternoon slots go to musicians who are being watched to see whether they are ready. The audience is the same audience that has been coming for forty years and it is not a forgiving one. Being programmed here in January changes a career.

locals: People attend two or three concerts in a day and do not consider this unusual. They arrive with the printed schedule marked up and leave halfway through one to reach the start of another, which is accepted behaviour and not rudeness. Tala is kept by hand in the audience by anyone who knows it. Families have a sabha the way other families have a football club, with a membership that predates the current generation. The canteen is discussed with the same seriousness as the singing, by the same people, on the way out.

localWord.translation: the Tamil month, and the obligations that come with it
localWord.body: Not a period so much as a set of things done: kolam on the ground before dawn, the temple before the light, and a concert season that fills the city until it ends.

changes: Music stops being an evening and becomes a working day. You start planning around start times rather than meals, and the question is not whether to go but which two to go to. The audience turns out to be the expert party in the room, which reorganises what you thought a concert was for.
start: Carrying the schedule. You start leaving a hall in the middle without guilt because the next thing begins in twenty minutes and everyone around you is doing the same. You eat at the canteen and then choose the following day's concert partly on the canteen. Within a week you can hear when the audience approves, because two hundred hands change at once, and you find you are listening for it.
stop: Waiting to understand it first. Nobody in the hall is going to explain the raga and none of the programme notes are for you. Chennai in January is running a season for people who already know, and the only way in is to sit through a great deal of it until the shapes start arriving on their own.
returns: An audience that is not being flattered. Nothing in the season is arranged to be accessible and nothing is shortened for anyone's attention span; a single item can run forty minutes and the room gets more attentive rather than less. It is the rare case of a city holding a standard in public and expecting you to come up to it.
remember: Nobody was performing for visitors. The room already knew the words.

items.label: September
items.body: The sabhas are dark and the halls are let out for weddings.

items.label: January
items.body: Several hundred concerts a day, and the canteen queue is part of it.

items.label: June
items.body: Forty degrees, and nobody sits in a hall for three hours.
